title: A new menu choice
summary: Route a new IVR choice to a new queue.
about: A lesson template (manual 9.4b). Each run picks a phone line with an IVR and a new menu choice that fits that kind of line (pick.choices, by a word in the workstream name; "*" for any other line) from the simulated environment, and fills in the {placeholders}: {choice}, {line}, {dial}, {workstream}, {menu}, {variable}, {suggested} (a queue whose agents fit the new work) and {fallback}.
finished: {choice} calls reach the right people now. Open the Diagram to see the route you built.
story: Contoso's {line} is answered by an IVR first. It asks callers what their call is about and sends them to {menu}.
This week the bot team added a new choice to the menu: {choice}. Nobody told the contact center. Your job: make sure {choice} calls reach people who can help.

tasks.title: Call the line and choose {choice}
tasks.do: Open the Phone tab, call the {line} and choose {choice}. Look at where the call ends up.
tasks.done: The call ended in {fallback}, the workstream's fallback queue: no rule knows about {choice} yet.
hints: Use the Phone tab. The line's number is already filled in.
After you choose {choice}, read the call trace: which step decides the queue?

tasks.title: Create a voice queue named {choice}
tasks.do: In the admin center, create an advanced queue named {choice} for calls.
hints: Queues are under Customer support in the site map.
Under Advanced queues, select Manage, then New queue. The type for calls is Voice.

tasks.title: Add at least two users to {choice}
tasks.do: Pick the people who will take {choice} calls. Agents from {suggested} know this work well.
hints: Select Add users, tick at least two people, then select Add.

tasks.title: Route {choice} calls to the {choice} queue
tasks.do: Add a route-to-queue rule to the {workstream} workstream: when the caller chose {choice}, route the call to {choice}.
hints: Rules belong to a workstream: open Workstreams, then {workstream}, then its ruleset under Route to queues.
Select Create rule. Under Conditions, select Add, then Add row. The IVR stores the caller's choice in {variable}; the value for {choice} is {choice}.

tasks.title: Test it: call again and choose {choice}
tasks.do: Call the {line} again, choose {choice}, and check where the call goes now.
tasks.done: {choice} calls now wait in their own queue, where people can answer them. Open the Diagram to see the new route.
hints: If the call still ends in {fallback}, check the rule's condition: variable, value and queue.
